scope: Exercise the public AC1018 writeTableWithLegacyZeroOverrides wrapper under callback-local allocation failure and invalid-value refusal in ASCII and Binary.

source.profile: One generated one-column, one-row ACAD_TABLE using a one-byte zero legacy override mask; no external or committed drawing fixture is used.

implementation.method: Extend the existing allocation fault probe to choose either writeTableWithLegacyZeroOverrides or writeTableWithLegacySourcePresence. Calibrate and inject one-shot bad_alloc at every measured callback offset. Require whole-file fileExport refusal, unchanged source identities and TABLE body, prior destination preservation, same-adapter retry producing byte-identical clean output, and fresh typed TABLE readback. Also pass mask byte 2 through the wrapper and require atomic refusal, unchanged caller and destination, then corrected same-adapter retry with {0} and typed readback. The wrapper validates the zero mask and delegates to the source-presence route; whole-file refusal remains authoritative because some caught serializer failures leave the callback emitted flag set while the writer sticky error prevents publication.

validation.directRun: PASS; source-presence API and zero-overrides API each passed 11/11 ASCII and 11/11 Binary allocation offsets; invalid mask byte 2 refused atomically and corrected same-adapter retry/readback passed in ASCII and Binary

limitations: Generated AC1018 transaction and typed-readback evidence only; no source-specific legacy spelling semantics, producer prevalence, or native TABLE behavior is established.

Only a one-cell zero mask and invalid byte value 2 are covered through the wrapper. Other invalid/nonzero masks, block-cell source presence, attributes, merged cells, and other TABLE payloads are not covered here.
P6-G remains open pending the public-writer inventory and other uncovered transaction profiles.
No support claim is promoted and no drawing fixture is committed.
